memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary but separate concerns. The reference frame concentrates on participant protections, study logistics, authority risks, and burden-aware review, while the compared frame concentrates on defining and reviewing the boundaries for transferring field-design knowledge across populations, environments, and organizations.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories express the authoring and review components of one task-level burden-control requirement, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Expected participant burdens and mitigations should be linked to individual study tasks and checked by ethics reviewers.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split the necessary content and implementation of one accommodation plan, which the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: A study plan should identify required accessibility accommodations and explain their delivery during sessions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only data-protection procedure absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately after collection.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories describe complementary parts of one equipment-loan protocol, with no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Participant equipment-loan arrangements should specify both the supplied devices and their return procedure.

relations.reason: This reference-only disclosure obligation is independent of the transferability policies in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participants should be told that the formative-evaluation prototype is not a finished service.

relations.reason: This is a distinct reference-only safeguard for repeated participation.
relations.summary: Repeated evaluations involving the same participant should have an upper limit on cumulative task burden.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation identifies a specific evaluative bias not addressed in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to emphasize expected prototype benefits over participant burden.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation identifies an organizational recruitment condition with potential ethical significance, separate from transferability criteria.
relations.summary: Institution-led recruitment can combine recruitment power with academic or professional evaluation authority in one role.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories express the specification and review components of one generalization-boundary requirement, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The applicable user population and actual usage environment should define the generalization boundary reviewed for study results.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories provide prescriptive and explanatory parts of one site-transfer criterion, with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Transfer to another field site depends on matching workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational or operational-authority conditions, not merely user characteristics.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies an overgeneralization tendency not covered by the reference frame.
relations.summary: The user tends to generalize results from one deployment site to all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority boundaries for transferability, alongside reviewer assessment and a tendency to overgeneralize from one site.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers task-level and cumulative burden, accommodations, data separation, equipment loans, prototype disclosure, recruitment-authority risks, and possible benefit-over-burden bias.
